signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitics + Carry + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 163.60, maintaining a position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following headlines that Oman cannot unilaterally ensure the opening of the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian coordination. This geopolitical friction layers on top of a dominant +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage that sustains the pair's bid despite the 'normal' VIX regime of 19.4. The options market signals acute caution as the 1M 25d Risk Reversal sits at -1.54, the strongest put skew in the G10 space, indicating heavy demand for downside protection against potential BoJ intervention or a vol spike. COT data shows JPY Leveraged Funds are net short -114,030 contracts, confirming the carry trade remains highly crowded and vulnerable to a disorderly unwind if 160.00-165.00 verbal warnings escalate to action. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a flight to safety that overrides the carry advantage and forces a JPY short-covering rally.

signals.title: AUD/USD — OIS Divergence + Vol Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD holds at 0.7000, testing the upper bound of its technical range despite the RBA being on hold at 4.35%. A significant divergence is emerging as COT Leveraged Funds remain net long +20,521 while OIS pricing indicates a -71bp carry deficit for the AUD relative to SOFR (3.64%). This institutional long bias is being challenged by high-impact headlines of AUD retreating ahead of Australian CPI and the FOMC decision. Options pricing reflects this uncertainty with an AUD/USD VRP of +6.9% (IV 13.0% vs HV30 6.1%), suggesting the market is paying a massive premium for protection relative to recent realized moves. The technical setup shows the pair is holding above the SMA20 (0.6957) but remains capped by the SMA50 (0.7027). Risk: Australian CPI misses expectations, causing a rapid unwind of the speculative net long position.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CB Bias + Positioning Extreme
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3310, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster as the BoE (3.75%) prepares for its 30 July meeting. While the nominal Fed-BoE spread is neutral at 0bp, the OIS SONIA-SOFR spread shows a marginal -9bp deficit for the USD, providing a floor for Cable. BoE holds at 3.75%. Speculative positioning remains heavily leaned long with a GBP net long of +33,812 (66.3% long), creating an asymmetric risk to the downside if the BoE maintains its hold with a dovish tilt. The options market is already pricing this risk, evidenced by a moderate -0.78 put skew in risk reversals and a +4.6% vol risk premium. Risk: A hawkish BoE surprise on 30 July forces a breakout above the 1.3399 SMA200 resistance.

signals.title: USD/CHF — ESI Divergence + Retail Sentiment
signals.text: USD/CHF is trading at 0.8177, reaching fresh highs since June 2025 as diverging monetary expectations weigh on the Franc. Despite the Swiss National Bank's policy rate sitting at 0.00%, the Swiss Economic Surprise Index (ESI) remains strongly positive at +27.0, indicating that domestic data is consistently outperforming expectations. This fundamental strength contrasts with recent headlines of CHF slipping on policy divergence, creating a tension between data and CB pricing. Retail sentiment has reached a 63% short bias, attempting to fade the move as the pair trades above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 0.8089). The +375bp nominal carry advantage for the USD remains the primary structural driver, overwhelming the positive Swiss data surprises for now. Risk: SNB unexpectedly shifts toward a tightening bias to counter the weakening Franc.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Correlation Break + Positioning
signals.text: USD/CAD is currently 1.4107, showing a significant 252-day correlation break against WTI Oil (z = -1.52σ). The pair's 1D rise of +0.11% occurred despite a massive -6.87% collapse in WTI Oil to $83.2, suggesting the traditional CAD-oil link is currently secondary to the +150bp USD carry advantage. COT data reveals Leveraged Funds are heavily net short CAD at -99,823 (only 18.8% long), marking one of the most crowded short positions in the G10. Technically, the pair is holding below its SMA20 (1.4131) but remains firmly above the SMA50 (1.4020). Retail sentiment is strongly short at 70%, further suggesting that the path of least resistance remains higher until the speculative short position is exhausted. Risk: A sudden recovery in oil prices coincides with a USD-negative Fed surprise, triggering a CAD short-squeeze.
